CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2021
  7:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Transportation Commission will be held on Wednesday, SEPTEMBER 8,
2021 at 7:00 p.m. pursuant to the order of the Alhambra Transportation
Commission Secretary.

Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-08-21 and No. N-35-20 from the
Executive Department of the State of California and the County of Los
Angeles Department of Public Health Safer At Home Order, the Alhambra
Transportation Commission meeting will not be physically open to the
public, although the public may participate by video conference or
teleconference and some of the Commission Members may choose to
participate via video conference or teleconference.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Martin W. Ray
  Alhambra Transportation Commission Secretary

Notice No: N2M21-110
Posted:  September 2, 2021

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and quality
  services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive business
  environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-08-21 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive Department of the State
of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health Safer At Home Order, the
Alhambra Transportation Commission meeting will not be physically open to the public, although
the public may participate by video conference or teleconference and some of the Commission
Members may choose to participate via video conference or teleconference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Webinar as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:

8656 or 1-301-715-8592 or 1-312-626-6799 and entering Meeting ID 833 8366 8556 and Passcode:
810183. Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that
the meeting can proceed.
For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please email Commission Secretary at
mray@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m. prior to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on
and the phone number you will use when calling or the name you will use when logging into the
meeting. You should then call or log into the meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will
unmute you and announce you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless
that time is adjusted by the Mayor. If you do not have access to a computer please call 626-570-3278 to
request public comment.
As an alternative to speaking during the meeting, you can email your comments to the Commission
Secretary at mray@cityofalhambra.org by no later than 5:00 p.m. on September 8, 2021 to ensure that the
Director has time to print the emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into
the record by the Director, with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the
Presidents discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the conclusion of the meeting
based upon its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but will
not be read into the record.
Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
email or call mray@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-3278 who will use their best efforts to provide
reasonable accommodations to provide as much accessibility as possible while also maintaining public
safety. Given the challenges of teleconference and video conference meetings, all participants are
encouraged to email their comments prior to the beginning of the meeting.

PRESENTATIONS

1. Traffic Safety Review Alhambra Road from Garfield Avenue to Chapel Avenue

Staff will review the report that was prepared in response to a citizen request to review existing
conditions along the segment of Alhambra Road from Garfield Avenue to Chapel Avenue.

As a result of extensive field data collection and review of existing traffic conditions, it is determined that
the data obtained supports additional traffic calming measures along this segment of Alhambra Road
from Garfield Avenue to Chapel Avenue.

Recommended Action

It is recommended that the Transportation Commission review the report with the City Traffic Engineer,
listen to public comment and authorize staff to implement the additional safety measures outlined in the
report.

2. Traffic Safety Review Edith Avenue between Front Street and Shorb Street

Staff will review the report that was prepared in response to a citizen request to review existing
conditions along the segment of Edith Avenue between Front Street and Shorb Street.

As a result of extensive field data collection and review of existing traffic conditions, it is determined that
the data obtained supports additional traffic calming measures along this segment of Edith Avenue
between Front Street and Shorb Street.

Recommended Action

It is recommended that the Transportation Commission review the report with the City Traffic Engineer,
listen to public comment and authorize staff to implement the additional safety measures outlined in the
report.

3. Public Comments

Comments must pertain to the business of the Transportation Commission.  Kindly limit all oral

5. Adjournment

Adjournment to a regular meeting on Wednesday, November 10, 2021 at 7:00 p.m.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact Martin Ray, Director of Public Works & Utilities, either in person
at the Public Works Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone
at (626) 570-5067 during regular business hours.

SUBJECT:  TRAFFIC REVIEW FOR ALHAMBRA ROAD FROM GARFIELD AVENUE TO CHAPEL AVENUE

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

On behalf of the City of Alhambra, Transtech Engineers Inc. has completed a traffic review of Alhambra
Road from Garfield Avenue to Chapel Avenue. The City received a resident request to review existing
conditions along Alhambra Road and increase signage along this segment. The placement of all traffic
control devices is dictated by engineering judgment and based on guidelines found in the CAMUTCD
(California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices) and the CVC (California Vehicle Code). As part of
the traffic review the following items were reviewed: existing roadway conditions, 5.5 years of collision
history, peak hour counts and line of sight. Please refer to Figure 1 below for a vicinity map of the subject
location.

Alhambra Road - Within the City of Alhambra, Alhambra Road is an east/west secondary arterial.
Alhambra Road is 38-feet wide with a posted speed limit of 30 MPH and one lane in each direction
separated by a dashed center line. Parking is allowed along Alhambra Road along both sides of the street
except for red curb and on Tuesdays from 12:00 PM to 3:00 PM for eastbound direction and 8:00AM to
11:30AM for westbound directions due to street sweeping. Additionally, parking is restricted for all public
streets in the City of Alhambra from 2:00AM to 6:00AM every day. Per the City of Alhambra General Plan
Parcel Map, land use along this segment of Alhambra Road is primarily High Density Residential.

Garfield Avenue - Within the City of Alhambra, Garfield Avenue is a north/south principal arterial road.
Garfield Avenue is 54’ (feet) wide with a posted speed limit of 35 MPH. Garfield Avenue has two lanes in
each direction separated by a double yellow marked center line. Parking is allowed along both sides of
Garfield Avenue expect red curb. Additionally, parking is restricted for all public streets in the City of
Alhambra from 2:00AM to 6:00AM every day. Per the City of Alhambra General Plan Parcel Map, land use
along this segment of Garfield Avenue is primarily Office Professional south of the intersection with
Alhambra Road and High Density Residential north of Alhambra Road.

Chapel Avenue - Within the City of Alhambra, Chapel Avenue is a north/south secondary arterial road.
Chapel Avenue is approximately 38-feet wide with a posted speed limit of 25 MPH. Parking is allowed on
both sides of Chapel Avenue except red curb and on Tuesdays 12PM-3PM for southbound direction and
12:30AM-6:00AM for northbound direction. Additionally, parking is restricted for all public streets in the
City of Alhambra from 2:00AM to 6:00AM every day. Chapel Avenue has one lane in each direction
separated by a dashed marked center line. Per the City of Alhambra General Plan Parcel Map, land use
along this segment of Chapel Avenue is primarily High Density Residential.

RECOMMENDATIONS

As a result of extensive field data collection and review of existing traffic conditions it is determined that
the data obtained supports additional traffic calming measures along the segment of Alhambra Road from
Garfield Avenue to Chapel Avenue. The following measures that should be undertaken to increase driver
awareness of the speed limit along this segment are listed below and shown on Figure 4:

  1. Install CROSS TRAFFIC DOES NOT STOP (W4-4p) signs at the intersections of Alhambra Road with
  Stoneman Avenue (North and South) and Monterey Street (North and South) as per CAMUTCD
  2C.59 (Number of Signs – 4)
  • The addition of these signs will emphasize that only the minor street is
  stop controlled.
  • These signs shall be installed under existing STOP signs at the mentioned  W4-4p
  intersections, along minor streets (Stoneman Avenue and Monterey
  Street).

  2. Add PAVEMENT LEGENDS next to existing speed limit signs, for eastbound and westbound, “30”
  as per CAMUTCD Section 3B.20 (Number of “30” pavement markings – 3)
  • The addition of these pavement legends will provide additional
  emphasis to the regulatory signage, speed limit, without
  requiring diversion of the road user’s attention from the roadway
  surface.
  • There are currently no existing pavement legends along this
  segment.

  •  Pavement legends shall be installed adjacent to existing speed limit signs for eastbound
  and west directions.

3. Install 36x36” STOP AHEAD (W3-1) for eastbound and westbound direction approaching the
  intersection of Alhambra Road and Chapel Avenue (Number of Signs – 2), and STOP AHEAD legend
  markings (Number of STOP AHEAD legend markings – 2) as per CAMUTCD Section 5C.04 and
  Section 3B.20, respectively.
  • The additional of these signs shall be visible for a sufficient distance to permit the road
  user to bring the vehicle to a stop at the stop sign.
  • The stop ahead sign (W3-1) shall be installed approximately 460-feet
  away from the intersection of Alhambra Road and Chapel Avenue, for both
  eastbound and westbound directions.
  • The pavement markings shall be installed adjacent to proposed
  eastbound and westbound STOP AHEAD signs. CAMUTCD Figure 3B-23
  W3-1  presents examples of elongated letters for word pavement markings and
  dimensions.

4. Repaint in diagonal striping the existing crosswalks in high
  visibility paint for the west and south legs at the Alhambra Road
  and Chapel Avenue intersection.

5. Replace existing stop signs at the intersection of Alhambra Road and Chapel Avenue with 36x36”
  STOP (R1-1) signs (Number of signs – 3) at each leg, adding all way plaque
  (R1-3p) under each stop sign (Number of signs – 3), and adding posts in
  red reflecting tape. (Number of posts – 3)
  •  Adding reflective signs and post will increase intersection
  visibility during night time.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The City of Alhambra received a resident request to assess existing conditions along the segment of Edith
Avenue between Front Street and Shorb Street. According to the resident, vehicles are driving along this
segment exceeding the speed limit. The resident is specifically asking for speed humps or additional
signage informing drivers of the speed limit. As part of the traffic review the following items were
reviewed: existing roadway conditions, 6.25 years of collision history, and output from a 24-hour radar
speed sample.

EXISTING CONDITIONS

Edith Avenue: Per the City’s General Plan, Edith Avenue is considered a residential road with a prima
facie speed limit of 25 mph. Edith Avenue runs north/south and is approximately 32-feet wide with no
center line with parking allowed on both sides of the street except during street sweeping hours on Fridays
NOON to 3PM for northbound direction and Fridays 8:00AM to 11:00AM for southbound direction.
Additionally, parking is restricted for all public streets in the City of Alhambra between 2:00AM to 6:00AM
every day. Land use along this section of Edith Avenue is primarily medium-density residential.

Front Street: Per the City’s General Plan, Front Street is considered a collector road with a posted speed
limit of 30 mph. Front Street runs east/west and is approximately 34-feet wide with a dashed yellow
center line with parking allowed on both sides except during street sweeping hours on Fridays 8:00AM
to 11:30AM for eastbound direction and Fridays NOON to 3:00PM for westbound direction. Additionally,
parking is restricted for all public streets in the City of Alhambra between 2:00AM to 6:00AM every day.
Land use along this section is primarily medium-density residential.

Shorb Street: Per the City’s General Plan, Shorb Street is considered a residential road with a prima facie
speed limit of 25 mph. Shorb Street runs east/west and is approximately 32-feet wide with no center
line with parking allowed on both sides of the street except during street sweeping hours on Fridays
NOON-3:00PM for eastbound direction and Fridays 8:00AM to 11:30AM for westbound direction.
Additionally, parking is restricted for all public streets in the City of Alhambra between 2:00AM to
6:00AM every day. Land use along this section is primarily medium-density residential.

TRAFFIC CALMING DEVICES AND STRATEGIES

Traffic calming is the process of reducing vehicle speeds through the use of both passive devices, such as
signs and striping, and physical devices such as changes in road elevation or path. As part of this study,
traffic speeds, accidents and traffic volumes were used to assess existing conditions along this segment.
The type, design and placement of traffic calming devices depend upon the road classification, desired
traffic speed and types of traffic issues along Edith Avenue. The following is a list of common traffic
calming measures usually deployed to reduce speeding, increase visibility of signs, decrease running of
Stop signs. This includes additional signage and pavement legends, beacons on Stop Signs, speed limit
signs and radar speed feedback signs as well as side stripes to visually narrow the travel lanes.

1)  Traffic Education Campaign
2)  Signage and Pavement Legends
3)  Larger Dimension Signs or Beacons on Signs
4)  Traffic Striping
5)  Radar Feedback Signs
6)  Targeted Police Enforcement
7)  Speed Humps: Since there are liability issues as well as impacts to street sweeping, trash trucks,
  emergency vehicle response and noise with the installation of Speed Humps the City of Alhambra has
  elected to not install speed humps on public streets. Speed humps can be placed in private parking

RECOMMENDATIONS

As a result of extensive field data collection and review of existing traffic conditions it was determined
that the data obtained supports additional traffic calming measures along the segment of Edith Avenue
from Front Street to Shorb Street. The following measures will increase driver awareness of the speed
limit along this segment. The improvements are listed below and shown on Figure 5:

1.  Adding 30”x36” SPEED LIMIT signs (R2-1) at each end of this segment, for northbound and
  southbound direction, 25MPH. CAMUTCD Section 2C.59 (number of signs – 2)
  • Remove existing speed limit sign at the north end of the segment (southbound
  direction) and install larger new 30”x36” at the same location.
  • The addition of these signs will provide advanced speed limit reminders for
  vehicles entering the segment of Edith Avenue from Front Street to Shorb
  Street.  (R2-1)
  • The speed limit signs shall be installed approximately 150-feet south from the
  intersection of Edith Avenue and Front Street for southbound direction, and approximately
  150-feet north from the intersection of Edith Avenue and Shorb Street for northbound
  direction.
2.  Add PAVEMENT LEGENDS next to proposed speed limit signs, for northbound direction, “25”.
  CAMUTCD Section 3B.20 (number of “25” pavement markings – 1)
  • The addition of these pavement legends will provide additional
  emphasis to the regulatory signage, speed limit, without requiring
  diversion of the road user’s attention from the roadway surface.
  • There is an existing pavement legend for southbound traffic 150-feet
  south of the intersection of Edith Avenue and Front Street.

  speed limit sign, approximately 150-feet north from the intersection of Edith Avenue and

3.  Replace existing STOP SIGN (R1-1) with 36”x36” Stop sign and add “CROSS TRAFFIC DOES NOT
